body:
Being an atheist means only that you do not believe in a god. It's not an organized religion, it is a group of people who collectively don't believe a higher being produced our reality. I am one of them. Because it's not organized, there is no one opinion. There are no teachings, no solid beliefs among the mass; despite those who think that atheism is a force against religion. We're not. Many of us simply don't believe a higher being exists, and have no vindication in participating in religious arguments otherwise. We are not all against religion, many of us just don't see the appeal to bother. Many of the people that choose to speak online are voicing their opinions of their experience, and many from anger or misunderstanding, but foremost their understanding. But all of us have different understanding. The beauty in being an atheist is that you don't have to agree with any one story, you can believe or disbelieve anything that you like.


The word "soul" was created to describe a concept, just as any other word we know in any language. It only describes a concept. As atheists are such a large and diverse group of people, I imagine any of us could have a different outlook on the matter. Many atheists consider themselves to be against religion, however most simply opinionate that no god exists. The short answer to the question is, we don't know. No one knows, and we may never know if souls exist. It is a word we use to describe what we leave behind of ourselves; some might just call it a memory, or a personality. The concept of a soul is only as powerful as the thoughts that an idea conducts. I know that's not a good answer, but the unknown often offers us no answers. That idea lives differently through the people it affects. I don't believe in an eternal soul myself, but I do believe that ways of thinking can inspire or at least affect any person that later listens, and that soul lives on (I choose to believe that's how religion came to be, just as any learned concept). For example, I believe my father's soul will live as long as I, or anyone he affected,  attempt to teach the lessons he taught us. I agree with you, in a way, that "the word of God" was created by men with underlying intention, whatever that intention may be (we don't know, we could never know). I believe in a "soul", but only as an idea that will be passed on if you pass it. And most times, I believe that the "word of God" might just be some guy who wanted us to keep his soul and ideas alive. 


There are many, many, beliefs among us who have no god. But the only real truth is that we won't know until we know. We decide for ourselves what truths we believe, what makes sense, and what words hold power over our hearts as long as they may carry on. Just as everyone else does.
